application_guidance.input_pattern: A projected Exp step and a comparison point in the same closed geodesically convex set.
read_original_when: Using a retraction, approximate projection or a manifold outside the standing Hadamard setting.
Requiring a complete verification of the triangle-comparison or projection dependencies.
sensitive_conditions: Hadamard geometry and exact nonexpansive metric projection.
The curvature factor uses the comparison distance; replacing it by a uniform domain value is an additional bound.

content.intended_use: Convert a tangent inner product into squared-distance decrease and a curvature-weighted step penalty.

proofs.locator: PDF p.8 Corollary 8 Eq. (7); p.9 first Proof
map: Set y=Exp_{x_s}(-eta_s g_s). In triangle (x_s,y,x), put b=d(x_s,y)=eta_s||g_s|| and c=d(x_s,x). Its angle A at x_s satisfies bc cos A=<-eta_s g_s,Log_{x_s}(x)>.
Lemma 5 Eq. (5) gives d(y,x)^2 <= zeta(kappa,c) eta_s^2||g_s||^2+c^2-2 eta_s<-g_s,Log_{x_s}(x)>.

Because P_X(x)=x, Lemma 7 implies d(x_{s+1},x)<=d(y,x). Substitute this smaller squared distance on the left and rearrange, dividing by 2 eta_s>0, to obtain Eq. (7). Degenerate triangles are interpreted continuously.
proofs.omitted_details: The three steps above paraphrase the complete short source Proof, rather than assert a new local Theorem. Lemma 5's technical appendix Proof and the external Proof of Lemma 7 are not reproduced or independently verified; they remain source-internal/external literature dependencies located explicitly here.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read and visually checked Lemma 5 statement and its main-text sketch, Lemma 7 statement, and the complete Corollary 8 statement and Proof on PDF pp.7–9.

content.source_scope_note: No function, Lipschitz constant, minimizer, bounded-vector assumption, Oracle call count or Algorithm lower bound is asserted.

assumptions: All sectional curvatures of M lie in [kappa,0], for a finite kappa<=0.
x_s and the comparison point x belong to X; g_s belongs to T_{x_s}M; eta_s>0; x_{s+1}=P_X(Exp_{x_s}(-eta_s g_s)).
The Hadamard and closed convex projection conditions are inherited from section 3 and Lemma 7; the broad wording at the start of Corollary 8 is not used to remove them.
statement.objects_and_definitions: M is a Hadamard manifold with Riemannian distance d, tangent inner products and norms, exponential map Exp and inverse Log. X is a nonempty closed geodesically convex subset. P_X is its exact nearest-point projection. Define zeta(kappa,c)=sqrt(|kappa|)c/tanh(sqrt(|kappa|)c), continuously extended to 1 when |kappa|c=0.
statement.parameter_domains: kappa<=0 finite; eta_s>0; c=d(x_s,x)>=0. Neither a diameter bound nor an objective function is needed for the pointwise statement.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such space and set, every x_s,x in X, every tangent vector g_s and every positive eta_s. This is a deterministic pointwise inequality; g_s need not be a function subgradient.

use_restrictions: The source's projected statement is recorded in its standing Hadamard setting; no unrestricted Riemannian projection claim.
Source-linked Proof reading is not independent reproof of Lemmas 5/7.

summary: One-step squared-distance inequality for an exponential step followed by exact projection, in the source's standing Hadamard setting.
title: Curvature-aware projected distance inequality
use_when: Control a distance potential for a projected tangent-vector step; function convexity and bounded subgradients are not required for this geometric inequality.
